assessments.reasoning: GNU’s fdl-1.2.txt identifies the November 2002 edition. Bytes [3313,3591) define the notice-listed passages. Bytes [7003,8015) expressly include the second medium class and distinguish the mandatory cover provision from the recommended overflow arrangement.

challenge.method: Hold the notice constant at 100 and 101 copies. At 101, test printed copies, nonprinted copies in a medium commonly having printed covers, and a medium outside both classes. Then vary the notice and the available cover space.
challenge.results: Exactly 100 fails the numerical condition. At 101, either qualifying medium satisfies the medium condition. A medium outside both classes fails it. Even in a qualifying medium, a notice requiring no Cover Texts leaves this duty untriggered. If all texts cannot fit legibly on the relevant cover, carrying the texts remains required. Following list order for those that reasonably fit and continuing on adjacent pages is the advised arrangement.

limitations: Whether a medium commonly has printed covers and which texts the work notice designates are factual conditions.
The per-passage word limits in §1 leave room for several listed passages to exceed one cover’s capacity. Other §3 duties have separate wording.
reasoning: GNU FDL 1.2 §3 covers both printed copies and copies in media that commonly have printed covers. Above 100 qualifying copies, the work notice’s required front and back texts must appear clearly and legibly on their respective covers, subject to the overflow guidance.
